$comment: An example environment with invented values, declaring every setting of this server. Import it into the store with `npm run config -- import config.example.json`, then change what differs in your landscape with `npm run config -- set <key> <value>`. `npm run config -- keys` explains each key. Nothing here is a secret: the SAP password is never stored. deploy/kubernetes.example.yaml carries the same keys with the values of a hosted server (tests/deploy.test.mjs keeps the two in step).
$passwordFile: Absolute path of a file holding the SAP password, for a server without a terminal (docs/deployment.md). Leave it unset on a developer machine: the password is then typed at every start.

atc.$defaultVariant: Unset on purpose: the system check variant read at start is the default. Set it (to DEFAULT or a listed variant such as ZDEMO_DEV_PRACTICE) only to override the system's choice.

atcVariants.name: ZDEMO_DEV_PRACTICE
atcVariants.why: development practices: naming, performance, robustness checks run next to the Clean Core one

$customizingTables: The installation's own tables for adt_customizing, beside the SAP-standard list in data/defaults/customizing-tables.json (T000, T001, TADIR, ... are already there: a standard table listed here is skipped with a warning). Every option of an entry: why (required), keyColumns (the row key printed by usage sweeps), routineColumns (a column, or a regex matching a column family, and the VOFM group whose routine number it carries), fields (the only columns a SELECT may name; `*` then means exactly these) and filterOnly (columns allowed in a WHERE and never returned, such as a user id).

customizingTables.name: ZDEMO_REGION
customizingTables.why: state -> sales district map read by a demo order integration

customizingTables.name: ZDEMO_PRICING_RULE
customizingTables.why: demo pricing rules: which requirement routine each rule calls, read when a routine is retired
